issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem statement UML and the solution expect addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch between the template and the specified API will confuse students about the correct method to implement and can cause tests or expected usage (which assume the single-argument method) to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO: implement */ }. If input validation is desired, implement it inside the single-argument method or provide an internal/private helper that accepts a validation flag, but keep the public API consistent with the problem statement and tests.

issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with a different signature than specified in the problem statement and implemented in the solution. The UML and problem text require addGuestStudents(int), and the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int). The template instead declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), introducing an extra boolean parameter (and different parameter naming). This mismatch makes it unclear to students which method signature they should implement and prevents direct mapping from the UML/problem to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) to match the UML and solution. If input validation is desired, implement it inside that single-parameter method (e.g., check the int and ignore/throw on invalid values) rather than adding an extra boolean parameter to the method signature.
